### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19b77452d006e179a6f18d859423b44ca5778d80` — the merge of head `435089b80c232c67f8559d7cfb4867e837de7b73` into base `5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19b77452d006e179a6f18d859423b44ca5778d80 && git checkout 19b77452d006e179a6f18d859423b44ca5778d80
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613 435089b80c232c67f8559d7cfb4867e837de7b73 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613 && git merge --no-ff 435089b80c232c67f8559d7cfb4867e837de7b73

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5651647d82dea5ce18ad537d629c18e3dd27f613` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head-sha: `bf9ca7d7d064f08a1e49a8b8034398edaa010c25`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/member-tier-holders-complete.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/position-graph.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph-role-holders-complete.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/team-graph.ts + packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts, packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.ts (isMissingTableError), packages/core/src/utils/object-not-found.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (resolveObjectName), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (the OBJECT_NOT_FOUND precedent), packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts (ITeamGraphService), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/position-graph.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bu-tree-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/queue-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/recipient-membership-recompute.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approver-address.ts, content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx, .github/workflows/ci.yml (dogfood gate), scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

Read from the net diff `origin/main...pr29497` (merge-base `aca58cdb6`), six files, +569/−29, and the cited code on `main`.

1. **Sharing `TeamGraphService.expandRoleUsers` now rejects on a failed or incomplete `sys_member` read; before it answered `[]`.** Who catches, traced in the live tree: every production reach of `expandRoleUsers` is the `sys_member.role` limb of `PositionGraphService.expandPositionUsers` (position-graph.ts L114) and the exported `expandPrincipal('role')`. `expandPositionUsers` is read by `SharingRuleService.expandRecipient` (L2145) and by `OwnershipQueueService.expandSpecUncached` (L336). From `expandRecipient` the throw reaches: `evaluateRule` (boot backfill sharing-plugin.ts L237, rule-write reconcile L510, bu-tree-recompute L258, queue-hooks L231 — each under a per-rule catch that warns and leaves grants as they were); `evaluateAllRulesForObject` (per-rule catch, L1450); `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` (L1586; its two callers bu-tree-recompute L291 and queue-hooks L212 both catch and warn — this is the branch that used to diff against `[]` and revoke every grant, and it now revokes nothing); `evaluateAllForRecord` via `expandRecipientForRecord` (record-write hook, rule-hooks.ts; the hook's wrappers at L252/L273/L304 catch, so an operator's write is never failed). End caller: no 5xx anywhere on the sharing side; a warning line and grants left unchanged. **Right.** Note for ④: `evaluateAllForRecord` has no per-rule isolation inside its loop, so a position rule that now refuses skips the later-listed rules for that one record on that write (before, the same outage revoked that record's position grants instead). Degraded both ways; graded should-fix below.
2. **`expandPrincipal` (exported from the plugin-sharing index) has no in-repo consumer** outside its own test; its `role` arm inherits the refusal. This is a public-surface behaviour change of plugin-sharing and is what the changeset's BREAKING banner names ("the role expansion in sharing"). **Right**, and correctly declared.
3. **Approvals `expandMembershipTierUsers` now throws on a failed or incomplete read.** Callers in the PR tree: `resolveApproverSpec` (L2565 directly for `org_membership_level`; L2562 via `expandPositionUsers` L3272 as the position union's second limb) — inside the directory try, caught at L2620, `directoryFailure` recorded, the slot falls back to its `type:value` literal, and the new warning fires with `error`. `position:NAME` is actable by a holder through server-resolved `context.positions` (approver-address.ts `positionAddresses`, `heldSlot`), so the dev's "whoever holds the position at decision time can still act" holds; `org_membership_level:NAME` is override-only, as the docs already say. **Right.** Submit never 5xxes on this path. Three further reaches of `expandPositionUsers`: `reassignTargetRefusal` (L6252, the reassign door and the `user` approver check) — a reassign to `position:X` during a `sys_member` outage now throws the refusal (before: `[]` → a false "no one holds position" VALIDATION_FAILED, or a slate built from the assignment limb alone); the throw lands before the audit row and the mutation, so the request is unchanged. `assertReassignTargetIsNotSubmitter` (L6230) — before, `[]`.every(...) was `true` and produced a false "the only holder is the submitter" refusal; now the real error. `escalateRequest` (L7690) has its own catch → `[]` → literal → `reassignTargetRefusal` throws → `runEscalations`' per-row catch (L6695) warns and the next sweep retries. All three are loud-and-unchanged rather than silently wrong. **Right**, and better than before; the reassign door's error is a 5xx-shaped message rather than a VALIDATION_FAILED, which is acceptable for a read outage.
4. **The changed `resolveApproverSpec` warning.** The catch now keeps the message; the graph-type branch forks on `directoryFailure !== undefined`. One imprecision: the try also wraps `bounded()` (`filterApproversWhoCanRead`), so a cross-org read-filter failure is also reported as "a directory read failed". The error text is carried, so an operator can tell them apart. Nit, not a defect.
5. **OBJECT_NOT_FOUND for `sys_member` treated as absence (`membershipObjectAbsent`).** The engine raises it from `resolveObjectName` (engine.ts L11862) off the in-memory `_registry.getObject(name)`, before any driver or datasource is consulted; the envelope carries `object` = the name asked. No backend outage can produce it, so it cannot hide one. Attribution on `object === 'sys_member'` matches the `sys-metadata-repository.ts` L2934 precedent exactly. `isMissingTableError(err, 'sys_member')` passes `readObject`, so the #13440 callers gate is satisfied. **Right.**
6. **Completeness and termination of the keyset walk.** `keysetWalk` (types/src/keyset-walk.ts) seeks `id $gt cursor` ANDed under `$and` with the caller's `where`, `orderBy id asc`, `limit` 10,000. Each iteration either returns (short page, empty page), advances the cursor to a strictly different key, or sets `truncated` and returns (row without key; same last key or same first key as the previous page). So it terminates on any reader, and it is complete on any driver that honours `$gt` and `orderBy` — which is the platform guarantee keysetWalk already rests on for its other callers (approval-service L8460/L8482 use the same shape against the same engine). Memory driver admits `$and`/`$gt` (filter-refusal.ts L763). Both plugins check `walk.truncated` and refuse. The `where` key keysetWalk emits is the engine's canonical slot (`filter` is folded into it, engine.ts L16769); team-graph used `filter` before, so no behaviour change. Under 10,000 rows the first page is short and the walk issues one read — the new tests pin 1 read at 9,999 and 2 at 10,001. **Right.** (On a double that ignores the seek, the walk reports `truncated` rather than hang — which is why position-graph.test.ts's fixtures needed ids, see ③.)
7. **Nothing cached on failure**: `TeamGraphService.cache.expandRole.set` and `PositionGraphService.cache.expand.set` both sit after the awaited read. **Right.**
8. **Core untouched; no new export from any package.** Confirmed from the file list and `git diff`: `packages/types`, `packages/core` absent from the diff.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29362-role-holders-complete.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`. The PR publishes a behaviour narrowing with no change to anything a metadata author can write (no key, value, type or export moves). Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor`; `none` takes `patch`; "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". So `patch` is the right level, the title's `!` and the `**BREAKING**` banner are present, and the ADR-0087 marker `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is a category `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` lists. Declaration lines: in the PR body the key appears on exactly one line, line-initial, value `no (narrowing)` (body line 6); in the changeset on exactly one line, line-initial, the same value (changeset line 8), followed by `Metadata-protocol: none` (line 9). No second spelling of the key anywhere in either body. Metadata-protocol `none` is correct for this diff. The `Check Changeset` check-run on this head concluded `success`. Level axis MEASURED and right.

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Forced test edit, position-graph.test.ts**: the two fake `sys_member` fixtures (`MEMBERS`, `MEMBER`) gain an `id` per row; the diff shows no assertion touched (+6/−4, all fixture lines plus one comment). The cause is real: `keysetWalk` reports a last row without the key as `truncated` and `readRoleHoldersToCompletion` refuses a truncated walk. Accepted.
- **Dogfood readings.** The `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run on `bf9ca7d7` concluded `success`, but on this head the three `Dogfood Regression Gate (N/3)` shards and `Dogfood Verify CLI` concluded `skipped`: ci.yml L2391 gates them off `pull_request` and `merge_group` (THE TWO SPEEDS, #22998), and `check-shard-attestation.mjs --verify` passes a skipped leg when the `filter` job succeeded (it did), with zero expected attestations. So the gate on this head did NOT execute the dogfood suite; it neither confirms nor contradicts the dev's 4 failures (flow-runas x3, declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest x1). The dev's control leg (both src files restored to `aca58cdb6`, both plugins force-rebuilt, same 4 failures) is the only reading, and the dev disclosed its own caveat (the plugin-sharing `--absent` dist preflight exited 1 on a non-unique marker; the leg rested on the force rebuild showing 0 occurrences of the new symbols). I read it as a probable main-red, as the dev does. **Escalated to the seat**: read `main`'s latest full-battery run (schedule or push) for those two files before landing; the carrier is seat 3 per the dev's third out_of_scope entry.
- **Check-runs on the head at review time**: all completed runs concluded `success` or `skipped`; none `failure`. Still `in_progress`: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)` through `(7/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`. `Type Check · source gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` all `success`. The seat lands only on the fast set's completion.
- **Dev deviation: relay `pr_create` carries no assignees** — procedural, nothing to judge.
- **open_questions 1 (share vs local paging)**: the dev recommends A, keep `keysetWalk` plus per-site glue. **Confirmed.** Core's `readOrganizationMembersToCompletion` is keyed to `organization_id`, throws the 503 `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` and warns about `org_user_ids`; generalising and exporting it would widen core's public surface for two callers that already import the one public walker, and would flip the declaration to the widen-and-narrow arm. The per-site glue is ~25 lines each; the one true duplicate is `membershipObjectAbsent`, spelled verbatim in both plugins (nit, see ④). #29398 stays open and separate, as the dev says; its "monotonic id check" would contradict keysetWalk's recorded equality-not-order design.
- **open_questions 2 (OBJECT_NOT_FOUND as absence)**: the dev recommends A. **Confirmed**, for the reason in ① item 5: registry-raised, pre-driver, attributed on `object`, with the metadata-protocol precedent. Option B would make the two approvals integration compositions the dev names refuse, for no safety gain.
- **Same-family reads the dev lists as out of scope** (sharing `expandUsers` on `sys_team_member`; both plugins' `sys_user_position` limb; `holdsRole`/`teamHasMember` catch → `false`): the card names `sys_member` at the two sites, so leaving them is within scope. One more member of the family the dev did not list: see ④ finding 2.

### ④ Design judgment

The published spec on `main`, `ITeamGraphService.expandRoleUsers` (packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts L666): "Return all user ids that hold a role of `roleName` in `organizationId`." The contract declares completeness and declares no answer for a failed read. The implementation on `main` delivered at most 10,000 ids and `[]` on failure — an undelivered declared capability. This PR implements the declared capability (all holders) and makes the spec's silence on failure a refusal rather than an invented answer; it takes nothing declared away at the consumer. On the approvals side there is no published contract for the tier expansion; `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` documents the "expanded to nobody" warning for an unstaffed slot (L108, L427), which stays true, and a failed read now carries its own distinguishable warning. The narrowing is the spec's own refusal made real, not a capability retired at the consumer. The design holds against the code it cites; I tried to break it along the five callers and the walk, and found no must-fix.

Should-fix (none blocks; the seat decides whether any rides this PR or the family's close-out card):

1. **`evaluateAllForRecord` has no per-rule isolation** (sharing-rule-service.ts L1400–L1421). Now that a position rule's expansion can throw, one refusing rule skips its later-listed siblings' per-record reconcile for that write (the hook's catch keeps the write safe). Before, the same outage revoked that record's position grants instead, so this is a trade of one degraded answer for a milder one, and the rule-wide passes repair it. A per-rule try/catch in that loop, as `evaluateAllRulesForObject` already has, would finish the posture.
2. **The queue path still turns the same failed read into `[]`**: `OwnershipQueueService.expandSpec` (ownership-queue-service.ts L306–L313) catches any expansion failure, `warnOnce`s "contributes nobody until it can", and answers `[]`. A `queue` sharing rule whose queue has a `position` member spec therefore still has `revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients` diff against a set missing its position-derived members on a `sys_member` outage — the card's class, one hop further out. It is that service's own declared posture (ADR-0142), outside this card's two named sites, and the dev's out_of_scope list does not name it. Name it on the family close-out card beside `sys_team_member`, `sys_user_position` and `holdsRole`.
3. **`membershipObjectAbsent` is duplicated verbatim** in team-graph.ts and approval-service.ts. Acceptable under answer A to open question 1 (the alternative is a new public export), but it is the one copy that can drift; the close-out card may home it next to `isMissingTableError` if a third caller appears.
4. **Docs**: approvals.mdx names the "expanded to nobody" warning but not the new "could not be expanded — a directory read failed" line. The `Flag docs affected` check-run is green and the dev's `Skills-docs: none` reasoning holds for what is documented; a one-line mention is a docs follow-up, not a gate.
5. **Nit**: the directory catch in `resolveApproverSpec` also wraps `bounded()`, so a cross-org read-filter failure is reported as "a directory read failed". The error is carried, so it is readable; the wording could say "a directory or read-filter lookup failed".

The previous record was re-read as an input and re-judged, not inherited.

1. **Round 2: `SharingRuleService.evaluateAllForRecord` catches per rule** (sharing-rule-service.ts L1411–L1431). The try wraps `matchRecord`, `expandRecipientForRecord` and `reconcileForRecord` for one rule; the catch warns and the loop continues. Does a refusing rule keep its grants while every other rule still reconciles? Yes: `reconcileForRecord` is the only writer in the loop and it is never reached for the rule whose expansion threw, so that rule's `sys_record_share` rows are untouched; the next iteration starts clean, and the only cross-rule state, `pass` (type `RuleEvaluationPass`, L468), memoises nothing but the position activation ledger, while `expandRecipient` (L2106–L2160) constructs its `TeamGraphService`/`PositionGraphService` per call, so a failed read leaves no cache entry for a later rule to read. The method's one production caller is `recomputeRow` in rule-hooks.ts L180–L182, documented "never throws (a hook must not fail the write)", and all three hook wrappers (L252, L273, L304) already caught at `warn` with `[sharing-rule] hook evaluation failed`. Both are improvements. A `reconcileForRecord` write failure is now caught one frame earlier than before, at the same level, and the rule-wide passes (boot backfill, `evaluateAllRulesForObject`) repair it; this is the posture the sibling `evaluateAllRulesForObject` (L1453–L1472) already has. **Right.** One public-surface note: `SharingRuleService.evaluateAllForRecord` is a public method of an exported class, and a direct consumer that saw a rejection on `main` now sees a resolve with a shorter `results` array; the PR body names this, the changeset does not (nit, ④).

The `error` carries the refusal text from team-graph, which embeds the driver's message, so the operator reads the cause. Level `warn` is right by the AGENTS.md question: after the degradation the system is visibly smaller (a grant missing, which its recipient finds), nothing claims to have persisted, and the whole-rule passes repair; the hook already logged this class at `warn`. No tracker number in the runtime string (`check:doc-authoring`). **Right.**
3. **The approvals warning wording** (approval-service.ts L2697): `could not be expanded — a directory or read-filter lookup failed`. The try (L2582–L2620) wraps `bounded(...)` around the department, position, org_membership_level and queue expansions and `expandTeamUsers`'s own tenancy screens, so the catch does take read-filter failures. The wording now matches what the catch covers; `error` is still carried; the integration pin was tightened to the new phrase. **Right.**

### ④ Design judgment

The published spec on `main`, `ITeamGraphService.expandRoleUsers` (sharing-service.ts L666): "Return all user ids that hold a role of roleName in organizationId." It declares completeness and is silent on failure. `main` delivered at most 10,000 ids and invented `[]` on failure; this head delivers all holders and refuses on failure. Nothing declared is taken from the consumer; the spec's own silence becomes a refusal rather than a wrong answer. `ISharingRuleService.evaluateAllForRecord` (L617–L622) declares "re-checks every active rule for object against this single record and upserts/reconciles only that record's share rows"; the per-rule catch is what lets it keep doing that for every rule when one cannot be read, and it matches the posture its sibling `evaluateAllRulesForObject` already publishes. I tried to break the new catch along the memo (`pass` holds only `positionActive`), the graph caches (constructed per `expandRecipient` call), partial `reconcileForRecord` writes (idempotent, repaired by the rule-wide passes, same level as the hook's existing catch), the `results` consumer (the hook discards it) and the multi-record `afterUpdate` loop (now strictly better). No must-fix.
